content.text:
The figure is finished in `index.html` and renders without console errors. It shows ISO years 2012–2026, one per row. Most years follow the same winter-high, summer-low cycle. 2020–2022 break that pattern: 2021 is low all year, and in 2022 the peak comes early, in December, and is much higher than usual.

```
REPORT
deliverable: index.html
requirements:
  R1: done - rows are ISO years 2012–2026 from the data, top to bottom
  R2: done - one cell per ISO week 1–53; the week count per year comes from the ISO week of 28 Dec, so week 53 shows in 2015 and 2020
  R3: done - sequential YlOrRd colour scale with a gradient legend labelled "ARE consultations per 100,000 population per week"
  R4: done - weeks before 2012-W40 and after 2026-W43 have no cell; weeks inside that range with no data would show as a grey outline, never as zero
  R5: done - week ticks (1, 4, 8, …, 52, 53) along the bottom; year labels on the left
  R6: done - title plus a one-sentence caption whose counts and year are computed from the data
assumptions:
  - The year and week are taken from the Kalenderwoche field (YYYY-Www), not from Saison
  - "Complete years" in the caption means ISO years with every week reported (2013–2025)
  - The caption counts winter peaks as weeks 40–13 and summer lows as weeks 22–39
  - The colour scale is linear from 0 to the largest value in the data
limitations:
  - The 2022 December peak (about 3,000) stretches the colour scale, so differences between ordinary years look smaller
  - Rows run January to December, so each winter wave is split across two rows (end of one row, start of the next)
  - The caption's "lowest average level" year is computed; its words about timing and height varying are fixed text
  - Tooltips work on hover only; the static image shows no exact values
```
